note: Set A gives an internally consistent reading of the stacked bars: a thin glass_biax layer of about 3 mm on top of a medium_density_foam core whose thickness decreases from roughly 42-43 mm at SNL-FFA-W3-500 15% to 13 mm at FFA-W3-211 77%, matching the plotted bar totals. Set B instead attributes the large core thicknesses (13-42 mm) to CarbonUD, a layer with no visible black segment of that size, and states every web0 glass_biax value twice with conflicting values (3 mm and 4 mm). Set B also omits most web1 data that Set A captures. Set A is clearly the better set despite skipping the 64% and 100% span positions.
remarks: Both sets quote stitched text-layer fragments (labels and percentages) that cannot literally contain the numeric values, since the values exist only as bar heights in the figure; this affects both equally. Exact bar values are only readable to within a millimetre or two from the image, so small discrepancies (e.g. Set B's foam 40/35/30/10 vs Set A's 43/38/33/13) were not counted as errors on their own. Set A omits the FFA-W3-241 64% and FFA-W3-211 100% positions entirely; Set B covers 64% and 100% for web0 but drops most web1 series. The circular 0%/2% columns appear to have zero or near-zero layup thickness and are unclaimed by both.
